study type: Mixed-methods (retrospective cross-sectional study and phenomenology/qualitative content analysis)
exposure: Not accompanied by partner during antenatal care visit
Belief in low probability of complications
Negative influence from immediate contacts (mother, mother-in-law)
cohort: Pregnant women who had antenatal care visits in Legambo District primary hospital and health centers in Northeast Ethiopia.
finding: Most pregnant women in Legambo district, northeastern Ethiopia, initiate their antenatal care visits late due to a combination of demographic (e.g., unknown LMP, no living children), geographical (e.g., distance to facility), and socio-cultural factors (e.g., negative influence from contacts, traditional beliefs) and healthcare experiences.
cross-section timing: Retrospective analysis of medical charts of women who had antenatal care visits, examining the timing of antenatal care initiation during their pregnancy.
